units.text: INT. ABANDONED CURLING RINK - DUSK
A vast barn of a building, its ice long since gone to a grey, cracked sheet.
Rust-colored light pours through broken clerestory windows and lies in long bars across the floor.
Hanging from the rafters, a faded banner reads PROVINCIAL CHAMPIONS 1987.
TOBIAS WREN (60s, broad shoulders gone soft, a wool cap pulled low) kneels at the hack, one stone beside him.
His hands, thick-knuckled and patient, rest on the handle as if on a sleeping animal's flank.
Ten paces away stands his granddaughter, MIREILLE WREN (17, lean, wearing a team jacket two sizes too large).
She holds a broom she does not seem to want.
A radio crackles on a rusted bench.
A tinny announcer's voice leaks out.
And the final end goes to Saskatoon, who take the national title.
units.name: ANNOUNCER

units.text: Tobias does not look at the radio.
He sets the stone, and pushes.
It slides, slow and crooked, and dies far short of the house.
You pulled it.
units.name: MIREILLE

units.text: The ice is gone, that's all.
units.name: TOBIAS

units.text: She sweeps a few strokes anyway, out of habit, then stops.
Coach called. They filled my spot.
units.name: MIREILLE

units.text: Tobias nods, as if to himself.
He wipes the handle with his sleeve, slowly, front and back.
Cold in here.
units.name: TOBIAS

units.text: Yeah.
units.name: MIREILLE

units.text: Neither moves.
Outside, a truck idles, waiting.
Its horn gives a single polite tap.
She lowers the broom to the floor, carefully, as one lays down a sleeping child.
Then she walks toward the door.
At the threshold she turns.
You coming?
units.name: MIREILLE

units.text: Tobias lifts the stone, studies it, and sets it upright on the bench beside the radio.
In a minute.
units.name: TOBIAS

units.text: She goes.
The light on the floor dims one bar at a time.
